origin.description: A key-value store whose keys are strings and whose values are any R objects. Keys are stored as UTF-8 and do not enter R's global symbol table.

arguments.name: missing_default
arguments.text: Value returned by get() when the key is absent. The default is NULL.

origin.details: set, mset, get, mget, has, remove, keys, size, clone, as_list, and reset. New keys fill the last free hole in a buffer that starts at length 32, so keys() without sort is slot order, not insertion order. keys(sort = TRUE) and as_list(sort = TRUE) order by Unicode code point. A stored NULL is present; an absent key returns missing_default.
origin.value: A list of functions closing over the map.
origin.example: m <- fastmap(); m$set("x", 100); m$set("letters", c("a", "b", "c")); m$mset(numbers = c(10, 20, 30)); m$keys(TRUE); m$remove("x")

translation.description: A key-value store from Unicode strings to any object. The string-to-index lookup is the Rust kernel; the hole stack that decides key order stays in Python.

arguments.name: missing_default
arguments.text: Value returned by get() when the key is absent. The default is None.

translation.details: set, mset, get, mget, has, remove, keys, size, clone, as_list, and reset. New keys take the last free hole in a buffer of length 32. keys(sort=True) orders by Unicode code point. None is a stored value; an absent key returns missing_default.
translation.value: A FastMap. Call methods with Python syntax.
translation.example:
from fastmap.fastmap import fastmap
m = fastmap()
m.set("x", 100)
m.set("letters", ["a", "b", "c"])
m.mset(numbers=[10, 20, 30])
print(m.keys(sort=True))
print(m.remove("x"))
